title: When should a water utility run its lake pump, and how much of the saving is the tariff?
lede: Pump scheduling on EPANET's Net3 (WNTR): running the lake pump 21 h from 01:00 cuts pumping energy 52 % at a flat tariff because it idles the booster pump; the time-of-use tariff adds 0 to 16 % of cost on top at a ratio of 3 (simulated, assumed tariff shapes).
summary: WNTR simulates Net3 for three days with pump 10 (the lake source) run in one daily window, 409 start and duration pairs, scoring the last day on pump energy (Net3’s 75 % efficiency) and time-of-use cost under three assumed tariff shapes with the peak/off-peak ratio swept 1.5–10. Feasible windows keep the tanks in range and daily balance within 1 %; pressure never binds. At a flat tariff the best window (01:00, 21 h) uses 1,307 kWh a day against 2,728 as shipped, 52 % less, because Net3’s river supply is mostly gravity and the booster pump 335 only runs when tank 1 is low, so more lake pumping idles it: a saving that needs no tariff. Beyond that, knowing the tariff adds 0.1 % of shipped cost at ratio 1.5, 15.8 % at 3 and 95 % at 10 for a 16:00–21:00 peak, and less for a daytime or midday-cheap shape. One network, one window per day, assumed tariffs (none sourced), no demand charge, a 1 % mass-balance gap not traced.
